note: Automated candidate collection. Not reviewed under this publication's evidence standard. Promote entries to the reviewed radar only through the website's curation process.

items.comparator: Holyvolt says its automated lab is 10 times faster than conventional R&D; the release says adding AI closes the loop and moves 100 times faster, but gives no measurement method or explicit comparison baseline for the 100× figure.
items.quantitative_outcome: Exact wording: “Our automated lab already delivers results 10 times faster than conventional R&D, and closing the loop with AI lets us move 100 times faster.” The same release reports an internally consistent dataset of more than 500,000 physical cells tested at over 165 million cycles.
items.signal: Distinctive battery-materials data access and a measured lab-throughput claim: Holyvolt says its AI models are trained on Wildcat’s accumulated cell-test dataset and linked to automated experiments. The 100× claim is weakly evidenced; the data asset is the more distinctive signal.
items.source: Holyvolt press release distributed by WebWire

items.comparator: The company compares its design-and-selection phase with the typical process, which it says takes years; no named competitor, study, or controlled comparison is provided. Lab capacity is stated as 25 physical materials per week.
items.quantitative_outcome: Exact wording: “Where the design and selection phase of a new polymer typically takes years, polySCOUT brings it down to weeks.” It also reports a “proprietary, verified database with thousands of data points” built over four years, and a high-throughput laboratory synthesizing and measuring 25 materials per week.
items.signal: A proprietary, source-checked polymer-property dataset paired with physical validation capacity is a potentially hard-to-copy data-and-workflow asset. The time reduction is company-reported and lacks a disclosed measurement protocol.
items.source: TNO launch announcement, reproduced by Textile World

items.comparator: Against reports generated by single AI agents; human experts compared interpretations blind. The time comparison was against an estimate of months to a year for serial human analysis and literature review.
items.quantitative_outcome: The company reported that its agents analyzed a whole-brain genomic dataset and synthesized findings in 32 minutes, compared with an estimated months to a year for serial human analysis and literature review. In blinded comparisons, human experts preferred the reasoning-agent interpretations 75% of the time.
items.signal: AI agents analyzed PerturbAI's proprietary whole-brain genomic dataset; the company said the collaboration with OpenAI is expanding into joint drug-target discovery.
items.source: PerturbAI announcement distributed by PR Newswire; the source also says findings were published in a joint preprint and blog post.

items.signal: Therna showcased an AI RNA research workflow that checks hypotheses against its proprietary experimental data lake, reported to contain tens of millions of measurements across hundreds of thousands of synthetic designs and dozens of cellular contexts. The company said some other proprietary datasets remain reserved for internal programs and partnered work.
items.source: Therna Biosciences announcement distributed by Business Wire.

items.signal: Lonza and Onava announced a research evaluation agreement under which Onava can use Lonza’s GS Gene Expression System for experimental validation of AI-enabled biologics discovery. Data generated through the collaboration is intended to feed Onava’s subsequent design cycles.

items.comparator: Comparable customer interactions completed in about 40% of the time previously required; the source gives no named competitor or independent benchmark.
items.quantitative_outcome: The reported outcome was that comparable customer interactions “can be completed in around 40% of the time previously required.”
items.signal: AI assistant for buying car insurance, policy changes and payments, with a reported reduction in time for comparable customer interactions. This is a workflow benefit, but the source does not establish that it is hard for competitors to copy.
items.source: Insurewire’s deployment roundup (secondary report; original announcement not established in the available results).

items.comparator: A similar version developed without the risk-reduction measures; the article says the benchmark tested finding and exploiting software vulnerabilities in a controlled environment.
items.quantitative_outcome: “Kimi K3.1 Pro scored 81%” on Moonshot’s cybersecurity benchmark; “a similar version without the risk-reduction measures scored 90.5%.” The reported difference is 9.5 percentage points. This is a safety-related capability tradeoff, not evidence of a competitive operating advantage.
items.signal: The company-reported benchmark comparison measures how risk-reduction measures affect the model’s cyber capability. Results were not independently verified, and the story does not report a workflow, throughput, cost, or discovery-yield benefit.
items.source: Digital Trends, reporting Moonshot AI’s internal testing

items.comparator: Same benchmark and harness across 30 models; the article says Claude Haiku 5.5 ranked 28th, and was 8.3 percentage points below Claude Haiku 4.5.
items.quantitative_outcome: “Haiku 5.5 finds 9.3% of the malicious activity across 26 attack campaigns.” The reported coverage is 8.3 percentage points below Claude Haiku 4.5; no operational improvement is stated.
items.signal: Simbian reports a measured threat-hunting benchmark result with a defined test setup and comparator. It is a capability signal, but the result itself does not show an advantage for a cybersecurity company’s operating workflow.
items.source: Simbian, publisher and operator of the Cyber Defense Benchmark

items.comparator: Not stated; the source reports a reduction since deployment, without specifying a baseline period or comparison group.
items.quantitative_outcome: “a 25% reduction in customer equipment-related incidents” since deployment in April, according to the operator. The report does not give a comparison group or baseline details.
items.signal: AI-based fiber-network monitoring is being used to predict likely customer outages and enable preventative intervention. The reported incident reduction is a measurable operating benefit, but the source gives limited detail on measurement.

items.comparator: Laboratory measurements; no non-AI baseline or specific test conditions stated in the report.
items.quantitative_outcome: “initial lab measurements of AI-based uplink channel estimation demonstrated typical throughput improvements of 10% to 15%,” with gains increasing as radio channel complexity increased.
items.signal: AI-based channel estimation improved uplink throughput in lab measurements. This is a quantified technical capability signal, not yet a field-validated operating result; the source says field trials are planned.
items.source: TelecomTV, reporting Deutsche Telekom’s announcement; the result was also repeated in Nokia’s announcement

items.comparator: Voyager building management system’s prior alert volume; the article says the reduction was measured against the building’s baseline but does not specify the period or methodology.
items.quantitative_outcome: Honeywell says the result at Voyager is “up to a 90% reduction in unnecessary alerts related to the Building Management System.”
items.signal: Honeywell trained an AI model using its engineering knowledge to distinguish actionable alarms from noise at a customer site. The reported site-specific reduction and use of proprietary engineering knowledge are a potential differentiator; the source does not detail the measurement method.
items.source: Fortune, reporting Honeywell’s claims and describing the Voyager deployment

items.comparator: The source says the AI tool helped the program break a two-year plateau; it does not specify the exact comparison used for the reported 32% figure.
items.quantitative_outcome: “Accelerate energy efficiency savings by 32 percent per customer within targeted segments.”
items.signal: Pacific Power used AI analytics to identify eligible households and target an assistance and efficiency program. The reported per-customer savings are quantified, though the article does not describe the measurement method or comparator in detail.
items.source: Las Vegas Sun, reporting Bidgely’s account of Pacific Power’s award and program results
